messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUGgies!

We will be meeting this Thursday (2/20) from 10-noon virtually and in person in the DataLab classroom (Library 360). This is a group working session so come with your questions for our expeRts, or just bring your laptop and get in some distraction free R-coding time.

Have you ever crashed RStudio because you ran out of RAM (memory)? Or maybe your code takes hours or days to run? How about this, a collaborator can't get your code to run on their computer but you can't figure out why. D-RUG on 4/10 is for you! Elise will be demonstrating how to solve these problems using RStudio on the new UC Davis high performance computing cluster Hive. Hive is a high performance computing cluster (HPC) that everyone at UC Davis has access to, no buy-in necessary. In order to be able to follow along with the demonstration go to the HPC Onboarding Website <https://hippo.ucdavis.edu/Hive> for Hive and request OpenOnDemand access for the UC Davis HPC Sponsored Public Group (publicgrp). If you have trouble with this, come to this week's D-RUG or post on Discourse <https://d-rug.discourse.group/>.

Datalab will also be open for Tea Time Thursday afternoon.

D-RUG: 10am-noon, DataLab Classroom, Library 360, and zoom https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/96397082218?pwd=S0JXcW5hcUFkbTcwMHFQV1NVNkg3Zz09
Tea Time: 1-2pm, DataLab Classroom, Library 360

Please consider posting your questions to our Discourse <https://d-rug.discourse.group/> site in advance of attending D-RUG virtually. This helps us do a better job of answering your questions, and also keep a log of the types of questions we see frequently.

See you then,

Your D-RUG Coo[R]dinators

messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUGgies!

This week from 10-10:45am, Elise will be showing you how to run your R code on a super computer (aka the Hive high performance computing cluster). Hive is accessible to everyone at UC Davis regardless of lab or college affiliation. However you do have to request access which can take ~2 hours to get approved, so if you want to follow along on your own computer registering now via HiPPO <https://hippo.ucdavis.edu/Hive> is a good idea. Select "publicgrp" and "ondemand" access.

Running code on a supercomputer can give you access to more memory, more processing power and a standard environment that people from across the university can run code on (no working about operating systems and software compatibility)

messages.body_plain:
DataLab is looking for volunteers to help staff the VR and Virtual Reality Sandbox at Picnic Day this year.  We need people from 11:00-2:00 this Saturday in the lobby of Shields Library for shifts in blocks of a couple of hours.

You do not need any experience with VR or VR Sandboxes.  We’ll teach you everything you need to know when you come for your shift. It’s really fun getting to see people’s reactions to this wonderful booth as they experience VR for the first time.

If you can help, please email Pamela Reynolds  plrey...@ucdavis.edu

Best

Michele

Michele Tobias, PhD

Geospatial Data Scientist

DataLab: Data Science & Informatics

UC Davis Library

370 Shields Library

(530)752-7532

mmto...@ucdavis.edu

ORCID: 0000-0002-2954-8710 <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-2954-8710>

messages.subject: FW: #maptimeDavis Workshop: Hand Drawn Maps
messages.body_plain:
Hi geo and R people! Pardon me casting a wide net here, but this is an opportunity for a little fun while learning. Tomorrow (Friday) I’ll be teaching a workshop on how to draw maps by hand. maptimeDavis planned this as a break from all that’s going on. Yes, you’ll learn some things about maps and cartography, but the goal is to relax.  I will bring pencils, pens, and paper, but feel free to bring your own if you have favorite tools. You do not need any art or geospatial skills to be successful with this. RSVP here <https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScHMZF-hPnY3J6T0NAbkrGBxjP0Xsw1wwhJftdHBklnXiq3sg/viewform?usp=header> so we know how many to expect.

Details forwarded below.

Michele Tobias, PhD

Geospatial Data Scientist

DataLab: Data Science & Informatics

UC Davis Library

370 Shields Library

(530)752-7532

mmto...@ucdavis.edu

ORCID: 0000-0002-2954-8710 <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-2954-8710>

Pronouns: she, her, hers

From: geospatial Sympa List (request) <geospatia...@lists.ucdavis.edu> On Behalf Of Matthew Conner
Sent: Monday, April 14, 2025 5:33 PM
To: geospatial Sympa List <geosp...@ucdavis.edu>
Subject: [geospatial] #maptimeDavis Workshop: Hand Drawn Maps

Hand Drawn Maps

Date:4/18/2025 10:00-12:00

Location:The Physical and Data Sciences Building, previously known as PSEL (Physical Sciences & Engineering Library) Seminar Room (room 1025)

Description: In this workshop, we’ll explore drawing maps by hand rather than using digital tools. This skill is useful for helping you as a designer deeply understand an area, but it is also a method of self-expression. The fact that it can be fun should also not be minimized.

"After completing this chapter, learners should be able to:
Explain why drawing maps by hand is beneficial and when to use this format over digital methods
Implement a workflow for drawing maps by hand
Design cartographic elements for their maps
Find and use reference materials

Concepts Covered: Cartography, analog maps

Speaker: Michele Tobias, DataLab

Michele Tobias is a geospatial data scientist with a background in geospatial methods for ecology. Michele earned her PhD from UC Davis in Geography where she studied California’s sandy beach ecosystem with traditional phytosociological methods and innovative remote sensing tools and was a postdoc at the UC Davis Information Center for the Environment. In her current position as a geospatial data scientist at UC Davis DataLab, she applies geospatial tools to new avenues of research across disciplines.

Prerequisites: Participants need no previous experience to participate

The following materials are recommended to fully participate in this workshop:
Paper (at least 2 sheets)
Pencils
A sharpener if you’re using a wood pencil
Eraser (bigger than the one that comes on the back of your pencil)
Pens
Colored pencils, marker, or crayons (optional)
A device with internet access to look up reference materials

Whenever possible, #maptimeDavis Workshops will be recorded and posted on the  #maptimeDavis YouTube channel <https://www.youtube.com/@maptimedavis95616>. #maptimeDavis Studio will not be recorded to encourage open discussion. Weekly reminders will be sent on the  Geospatial Email List <https://lists.ucdavis.edu/sympa/info/geospatial>.

#maptimeDavis Workshops and Studio are a product of UC Davis DataLab’s  Spatial Sciences Research Cluster <https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/spatial-sciences/> and are supported by the contributions and participation of our community. Please send questions to Michele Tobias mmto...@ucdavis.edu

Matt Conner

Student Services Department

Library

University of California, Davis

on behalf of the #maptimeDavis council
